_comment: v10 Phase A.1 source-cycle table. One row per cited standard listing the publishing body, the current edition, the cycle in years, the next-expected release date (best estimate), and a free-access URL. Used by scripts/check-citation-freshness.mjs to flag manifests whose 'edition' string is more than one cycle behind the current publication of that standard. spec-v22 CF-03: when 'next_expected' is in the past, the row must carry a 'last_verified' (ISO date >= next_expected) re-stamp -- the 'verified, not yet released' acknowledgement -- or the freshness gate fails. Update on each rollover (see docs/citation-freshness-ledger.md). Since 2026-09-02 the file also carries `annual_figures`: the bundled federal dollar figures that reprice every year on a known calendar (IRS mileage, Section 179, the SSA wage base, FHFA and HUD loan limits, GSA per-diem, HUD FMRs, Pub 15-T). Five of them were found stale on one day; nothing had ever asked when their publisher last spoke.

standards.name: IUPAC/CIAAW Standard Atomic Weights
standards.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-09 against the publisher's own tables at ciaaw.org/atomic-weights.htm and ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm, both of which head the table "Standard Atomic Weights 2024" -- the Atomic Weights 2021 report with 2024 revisions to gadolinium, lutetium and zirconium. The shard previously declared edition 2021. Of the three revised elements only ZIRCONIUM is bundled, and it was stale: the shard carried 91.224 where the 2024 abridged table gives 91.222(3), confirmed on both pages. Corrected in the shard and in the runtime copy in calc-lab.js. Every other bundled value was spot-checked against the 2024 abridged table and is unchanged, the interval elements at their conventional values (H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, Mg 24.305, Si 28.085, S 32.06, Cl 35.45, Ar 39.948, Pb 207.2). CIAAW revises on roughly a two-year cycle, so recheck when next_expected passes.

standards.name: Manufacturer centrifuge-rotor radii
standards.verification_note: All six rotor rows verified 2026-09-09 against each manufacturer's own published figures, and against the radius those figures imply through RCF = 1.118e-6 x r(mm) x rpm^2 -- the inversion is what settles a radius the vendor does not print, since max speed and max RCF are always published. THREE OF THE SIX WERE WRONG. (1) FA-45-6-30 carried 95 mm, which is the FA-45-30-11's radius -- the same wrong-rotor copy the 5424 row made. Eppendorf's instructions for use give 12.3 cm without adapter, and both published pairs agree (16,639 x g / 11,000 rpm and 20,133 / 12,100 each imply 123.0 mm). Corrected to 123. (2) A-4-81 carried 162 mm, which is its MTP/Flex plate bucket (Eppendorf states 16.3 cm; 2,900 x g at 4,000 rpm implies 162.1) under a label naming the rotor generally. With the buckets it ships with -- 500 mL rectangular or 7 x 50 mL conical -- Eppendorf states 18 cm and its published 3,220 x g at 4,000 rpm implies 180.0 mm. Corrected to 180 and the label now names the bucket. (3) Fiberlite F15-8x50c carried 137 mm against a published 10.4 cm, so every RCF it gave was 32% high; Thermo publishes 14,500 rpm / 24,446 x g, implying 104.0 mm. Corrected to 104. The 5424 FA-45-24-11 (84 mm) and the two Beckman rows (JA-10 158 mm, JA-20 108 mm) were verified on 2026-09-09 and are unchanged. A unit test now cross-checks EVERY row against its published speed/RCF pair and asserts the covered set equals the shard, so an unchecked row cannot be added silently. FETCH NOTES: eppendorf.com 403s WebFetch but serves a plain curl with a browser user-agent; thermofisher.com needs the browser (cookie wall) and publishes speed and RCF but no radius.

standards.name: Laboratory buffer pKa values
standards.verification_note: All eight rows verified 2026-09-09. THE DEFECT WAS A TEMPERATURE, NOT A NUMBER: the table is keyed buffers_at_25C and the runtime comment said 25 C, but the four Good's buffers were cited to Good et al. 1966, WHICH TABULATES AT 20 C -- and two of the four carried his 20 C values (HEPES 7.55, MOPS 7.20) while the other two had already been carried to 25 C by somebody who stopped halfway (MES 6.10, PIPES 6.76). Corrected against the 25 C column of PanReac AppliChem's Biological buffers IP-022EN: HEPES 7.48, MOPS 7.14. Two independent confirmations: that table's own d(pKa)/dT carries Good's 20 C values exactly onto it (7.55 - 5 x 0.014 = 7.48; 7.20 - 5 x 0.011 = 7.14; 6.15 - 5 x 0.011 = 6.10; 6.80 - 5 x 0.0085 = 6.76), and Promega's technical reference publishes the same 20 C column with the same coefficients. IP-022EN also confirms Tris 8.06 at 25 C and every useful range the shard carries. The CRC rows (phosphate pK2 7.20, acetate 4.76, carbonic pK1 6.35) are unchanged and are 25 C values. A unit test pins all eight in both copies. RECHECK TRIGGER: not an edition cycle -- these are physical constants -- so the row exists to ask whether the temperature label still matches the values.

standards.name: Industry inventory-turnover benchmarks
standards.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-09 against the U.S. Census Annual Retail Trade Survey's own 2022 benchmarked tables (released 2026-08-31), and NOTHING IN THE ROW SURVIVED. (1) THE YEAR CANNOT EXIST: every row was stamped 2023. ARTS's last data year is 2022 -- the survey folded into the Annual Integrated Economic Survey, which began collecting in March 2024 -- and the ASM has no 2022 or 2023 data year at all, because years ending in 2 and 7 are covered by the Economic Census. (2) THE STATISTIC WAS MISNAMED: the key was turnover_median, and Census publishes industry AGGREGATES, not medians across firms. (3) THE VALUES DID NOT REPRODUCE: turnover = COGS / average inventory computes to 7.01 (retail total), 12.94 (NAICS 4451 grocery), 2.98 (448 apparel) and 2.67 (4413 auto parts) against bundled 8, 14, 4 and 5 -- auto parts was 87% high. COGS was derived two independent ways from Census's own tables and they agree to three significant figures: sales minus gross margin, and purchases plus the change in inventory. (4) TWO ROWS HAD NO PUBLISHER AT ALL: ARTS never covered food services (NAICS 722) and the SBA publishes no such median, so restaurant_food (26) cited nothing checkable; manufacturing_general cited an ASM year that does not exist. Both rows removed rather than left unbacked. FETCH NOTES: the ARTS xlsx tables download with a plain curl and a browser user-agent, EXCEPT sales.xlsx, which a WAF rejects -- sales can be recovered as gross margin divided by the gross-margin percentage, and the purchases route confirms the answer independently. The Census data API now requires a key, so use the table downloads.

annual_figures.name: HUD Fair Market Rents
annual_figures.verification_note: FULLY verified 2026-09-09: all 19 rows read against HUD's own FY2026 Fair Market Rent Documentation System in a BROWSER (huduser.gov serves no automated fetch -- curl and WebFetch both get an empty 202). The path: portal/datasets/fmr/fmrs/FY2026_code/select_Geography.odn?year=2026&fmrtype=Final&state=<fips>&statename=<Name> lists every FMR area with its cbsasub code, then 2026summary.odn?year=2026&fmrtype=Final&cbsasub=<code>&selection_type=cbsa gives the FMR table. A SMALL AREA FMR area's page shows only the ZIP table; its metro-wide figure is behind &dallas_sa_override=TRUE&selection_type=hmfa. WHAT WAS WRONG: 18 of the 19 rows carried figures matching neither HUD's FY2026 nor its FY2025 table (Dallas efficiency read 1,273 against HUD's 1,582; New York 2BR read 2,680 against 2,910), and FOUR rows named an area HUD does not publish -- Denver-Aurora-Lakewood (HUD: Denver-Aurora-Centennial), Austin-Round Rock (Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos), Honolulu MSA (Urban Honolulu MSA), and Houston ... MSA (Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land HUD Metro FMR Area). Only San Francisco, corrected on 2026-09-09, already agreed. All 19 names, rent sets and cbsasub codes are now pinned by a unit test. THE SAFMR DOUBT IS RESOLVED: 11 of the 19 are Small Area FMR areas where HUD sets every Housing Choice Voucher payment standard by ZIP, and Houston is one where a PHA opted in. Those rows now carry a safmr flag and the tile prints the advisory with the metro-wide figure rather than presenting it as the voucher standard.

annual_figures.name: IRS Pub 946 Table A-1 MACRS percentages
annual_figures.covers: tax year; Pub 946 is revised annually
annual_figures.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-03 against Publication 946 (2025), page 70, Table A-1 (half-year convention), fetched as irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf. All six recovery periods match value for value, including the 15-year 5.90/5.91 and 20-year 4.462/4.461 alternations and the 21st-year 2.231 stub. The percentages are statutory and have not moved since 1986, so the annual ask is whether the bundled TABLE is still the published table, not whether a rate repriced.
